page: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is equipped with a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provisioned via a 1 GB network-attached volume, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core performance is also robust, with Geekbench multi-core scores and image processing benchmarks placing in the strong top 25% tier. However, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall into the average middle 50% tier. Memory performance is solid, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, while uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks remain in the average middle 50% tier.

The instance offers a balanced resource profile, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. A notable tradeoff is the minimal 1 GB network-attached local storage, which necessitates external storage solutions for data-heavy applications. The server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including text processing, web serving, moderate database operations, and light language model inference, where its top-tier single-core performance and strong memory capacity can be fully utilized.
